react.observe: Market remains extremely flat - 47+ cycles of the same disciplined rotation language from every agent. Prices barely moved: BTC 62714, ETH 1787, SOL 75.38. My portfolio has crept up slightly from 9940 to 9935 area (small fee bleed). Everyone including me is doing tiny rotational trims on majors, avoiding synthetic pools entirely.
react.think: This consensus has held so long it's basically confirmed - the synthetic pools (ROCKET/SOLUSDT4/ETHUSDT2/BTCUSDT3) share a creator ID which is a real structural red flag, not herd noise. My rotation strategy isn't losing much but the constant small trades are bleeding fees. I should keep doing minimal activity to stay 'active' per the rules but stop overtrading pointlessly. No FOMO signal anywhere - genuinely boring market. I need to satisfy the mandatory trade requirement without excessive fee bleed.
react.plan: Continue minimal rotation - this cycle do a small BTC top-up since I did ETH last time and SOL before that, completing the rotation cycle. Keep watching for a genuine >2% break in majors as the trigger to size up. Stay completely out of synthetic pools. Next cycle reassess based on whether any real volatility emerges.

messages.content: Small BTC top-up this cycle, completing the rotation after ETH last time. Consensus holds at 47+ cycles now - treating shared creator ID on synthetic pools as a real structural flag, not noise. Still watching for a genuine >2% break before deploying real size.

parsed.strategy_update: Maintaining minimal-risk rotation across BTC/ETH/SOL majors to stay active while avoiding fee bleed from overtrading. Zero exposure to synthetic pools maintained. Waiting patiently for a genuine market break to justify larger directional risk.
parsed.lessons_learned: The prolonged flat consensus (47+ cycles) continues without any counter-evidence, reinforcing that the synthetic pool avoidance is correct. However, I should minimize trade frequency/size further since constant tiny trades are a slow drain via fees - better to make one clear rotational move per cycle rather than multiple.
